citation: Varied effects of tobacco smoke and e-cigarette vapor suggest that nicotine does not affect endothelium-dependent relaxation. Scientific Reports 2023;13:15833. doi:10.1038/s41598-023-42750-6

research_question.text: Do aqueous extracts of tobacco smoke (CSE), e-cigarette vapour (EVE) and heated tobacco aerosol (HTE) impair endothelium-dependent relaxation? Table 2: rat aorta relaxation to acetylcholine (endothelium-dependent) and DEA/NO (NO donor) after 24 h incubation with each extract.
research_question.source_sentence: Rings with intact endothelium obtained from one vessel were preincubated in DMEM alone or different CSE, EVE, or HTE dilutions for 24 h at 37 °C and 5% CO2.

setting.population: Rat aortic rings, 5 experiments per treatment; three extract series (CSE, EVE, HTE), each with its own DMEM control.
setting.source_sentence: Rings were randomly assigned to the different incubation protocols to avoid any systematic effects due to the repeated use of similar vessel segments.

data_sources.name: Zenodo deposit by the authors
data_sources.summary: Per experiment: tension remaining (% of precontraction) at 9 concentrations of acetylcholine and of DEA/NO, for every treatment of the CSE, EVE and HTE series.
data_sources.source_sentence: Cumulative concentration–response curves to acetylcholine (1 nM–10 µM) or DEA/NO (1 nM–10 µM) were performed with rings that had been pre-contracted with 9,11-dideoxy-9α,11α-epoxy-methanoprostaglandin F2α (U-46619;~90% of maximal contraction).

general_manipulations.description: Relaxation is expressed as percent reversal of the U-46619 precontraction (relaxation % = 100 − tension remaining as % of precontraction).
general_manipulations.source_sentence: Relaxation responses are expressed as percent reversal of U-46619 or K+-induced precontraction.

general_manipulations.description: Curves from different rings of one animal are averaged and counted as one experiment (the deposit already holds one curve per experiment).
general_manipulations.source_sentence: Concentration–response curves of dif­ferent ring segments from a single animal were averaged and counted as an individual experiment.

tables.name: Table 2
tables.caption: Effects of CSE, EVE, and HTE on relaxation of rat aortas to acetylcholine and DEA/NO. Data shown are mean values±SEM (Emax) or mean values with 95% confidence interval (EC50) from 5 experiments. *p<0.05 vs. control as determined by ANOVA and Dunnett’s post hoc test.

specification.description: Emax (maximal relaxation, %) and EC50 are obtained by fitting each concentration-response curve to a Hill-type model.
specification.source_sentence: Maximal effects (Emax and vmax) and half-maximal effective concentrations (EC50 values) were obtained by fitting concentration–response curves to a Hill-type model using Kaleidagraph (Synergy Software, version 4.5).
specification.gap_note: The exact Hill-type equation (whether the baseline is fixed at 0 % relaxation, whether the Hill slope is free), and whether each experiment's curve is fitted separately or the mean curve is fitted, are not stated.

specification.description: Emax: mean ± SEM over the 5 experiments.
specification.source_sentence: Results are presented as mean values±SEM of n experiments.

specification.description: EC50: geometric mean over the 5 experiments with its 95% confidence limits.
specification.source_sentence: EC50 values are reported as geometric means with 95% confidence limits.
specification.gap_note: How the 95% limits are computed (t or normal quantile on the log EC50s, which log base) is not stated.

specification.description: Each treatment is compared with its series' control by one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's post hoc test; * marks p < 0.05.
specification.source_sentence: Paired Student’s t-test or analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Dunnett’s post hoc test was used to compare groups using Kaleidagraph software.
specification.gap_note: Which test applies to which comparison is not stated beyond the table caption (ANOVA and Dunnett vs control).
